questions.def: Past perfect 'had' shows the action was complete before another past action.
questions.question: By the time he arrived, the movie ___ already started.

questions.def: Past perfect describes a state or action completed before a past time.
questions.question: I ___ him for years, but we lost touch.

questions.def: Past perfect describes an action completed before another past action.
questions.question: They ___ in London before moving to Rome.

questions.def: Present perfect 'has' + past participle describes an experience up to now.
questions.question: She ___ never seen such a beautiful sunset.

questions.def: Future perfect 'will have' shows completion by a future time.
questions.question: They ___ finished the report by Friday.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous: duration of an action up to now.
questions.question: I ___ for the bus for over an hour.

questions.def: Future perfect signifies completion before a future time.
questions.question: By next year, I ___ here for ten years.

questions.def: Present perfect describes experiences within a period up to now.
questions.question: We ___ to Paris three times this year.

questions.def: Past perfect signifies completion before a past event.
questions.question: They ___ the project before the deadline.

questions.def: Past perfect: Action completed before another in the past.
questions.question: He ___ just left when you called.

questions.def: Past perfect shows an action completed before another in the past.
questions.question: By the time I woke up, he ___.

questions.def: Use 'have known' as 'know' is a stative verb, not continuous.
questions.question: I am knowing him since we were children.

questions.def: Past perfect: the action of reading was completed before a past time.
questions.question: She ___ all the books by that author.

questions.def: Future perfect continuous: duration of action up to a future time.
questions.question: By 5 pm, she ___ working for eight hours.

questions.def: Present perfect: experience up to the present moment.
questions.question: I ___ never seen such a thing before!

questions.def: Use 'has lived' to show duration from the past to present.
questions.question: He is living here since 2010, and he's happy.

questions.def: Future perfect continuous: duration of an action up to a future time.
questions.question: By the end of the year, I ___ English for 5 years.

questions.def: Past perfect continuous: action duration before a past event.
questions.question: They ___ been waiting for hours when the train finally arrived.

questions.def: Past perfect: experience before a past event.
questions.question: Before I met her, I ___ to Japan.

questions.def: Past perfect: state existing before a past event.
questions.question: I ___ him for years before he moved away.

questions.def: Past perfect continuous emphasizes the duration before a past event.
questions.question: We ___ expecting you earlier.

questions.def: Present perfect 'hasn't been' expresses a state continuing until now.
questions.question: She ___ feeling well lately.

questions.def: 'Has worked' or 'has been working' are correct, not 'is worked'.
questions.question: He is worked here since last June.

questions.def: Future perfect continuous emphasizes duration up to a future point.
questions.question: By the time she retires, she ___ here for 40 years.

questions.def: Present perfect describes an experience up to now.
questions.question: I ___ never experienced such hospitality.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous emphasizes the ongoing search until now.
questions.question: They ___ searching for a solution for weeks.

questions.def: Future Perfect describes an action completed before a future time.
questions.question: By the time the guests arrive, we ___ all the preparations.

questions.def: Present Perfect connects a past action to a present result.
questions.question: She feels much better now that she ___ the medicine.

questions.def: Use Present Perfect Continuous ('have/has been knowing') for duration.
questions.question: I am knowing him for over ten years.

questions.def: Present Perfect Continuous emphasizes the ongoing nature of the action.
questions.question: He ___ on this project since last January.
